correctness.rationale: For 1<r<=sqrt(2), pairwise spike segments meet the unit ball, so the cited cap-body criterion applies. The cited vertex criterion reduces spike illumination to signed coordinate inequalities. In the subcritical range the displayed four unit directions cover all six spike vertices, have an exact positive dependence, and span R^3 because their determinant is s(3x^2-1) != 0; hence they positively span R^3 and illuminate K_r. The universal three-dimensional lower bound gives equality 4. At r=sqrt(2), one unit direction cannot have two coordinates of absolute value >1/sqrt(2), so six spikes require six directions, and the six coordinate directions attain the bound. All strict inequalities and endpoint cases are accounted for.

value.rationale: The parameter r=sqrt(2) is not an arbitrary slice: it is exactly the geometric tangency threshold at which the six axial base caps reach angular radius pi/4 and the classical sharp six-direction example occurs. Determining that every common inward radial perturbation collapses the illumination number from the class maximum 6 to the ambient minimum 4 gives a sharp structural boundary and an explicit optimal four-direction mechanism.
